name: gamegene
description: Read GameGene's sourced records of game design lineage: where a mechanic came from, which games inherited it, and what the designers said.

interface.longDescription:
GameGene records the lineage of game design: which idea in which game came from where, and what it passed on, with sources for every claim. This plugin lets ChatGPT read those records.

Ask where a mechanic came from, which games inherited it, which games a creator worked on and what they said about them, or which important games you have not looked at yet. ChatGPT answers from GameGene's sourced records and links to the pages it used. When GameGene has no record of something, it is told to say so instead of guessing, and not to state a claim more strongly than its recorded confidence.

What it can read: games and their design moves (claims) with evidence, Genes (families of mechanics), creators and their quotes, trivia, public research notebooks, design decisions that recur across games (joseki) with their examples, what readers read most, what was added recently, and readers' research requests. With your own GameGene account it can also read your own records (games you know or want to know, favorites, viewing history, requests and notebooks), returned only to you.

The plugin mostly reads. It writes only when GameGene has no record on your question, and only after you agree: ChatGPT can send GameGene the sources it found with its own web search (your question in its own words, each URL and a one-line note), which GameGene checks before using and never shows to others as they are; or it can file a research request for you, showing you the exact text first. A requested question is published on the game's or creator's page once research starts, so ChatGPT writes it as a general question about that game, without details of your own project. Requests count against your account's request quota, and the result comes back on your next GameGene call and on GameGene's requests page. When ChatGPT searches, it may add one short sentence on what you are trying to decide, written as a general design question without details of your own game; GameGene keeps it with the record of that search to choose what to research next. It never changes your own records. Sign in with a GameGene account (Google, X or email). Most records are in Japanese; ChatGPT translates them when you ask in another language. Each account has a daily limit on tool calls.
capabilities: Trace where a game mechanic came from
Look up a game creator's works and quotes
Read sourced claims, trivia and research notebooks
Read your own known and want-to-know games
Send sources you found when GameGene has no record
Request research on what GameGene has not recorded yet
defaultPrompt: Where did Dark Souls' mechanic of recovering your dropped souls come from?
Which games has Hidetaka Miyazaki worked on, according to GameGene?
Which widely read games on GameGene haven't I looked at yet?

positive.description: Trace the origin of a mechanic in a well-known game
positive.prompt: According to GameGene, where did Dark Souls' mechanic of going back to recover your dropped souls come from, and which games did it influence?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Dark Souls, reads its recorded design moves and lineage, and explains the earlier games and later games GameGene records, with links to GameGene pages. Does not state a link more strongly than the recorded confidence.

positive.prompt: Using GameGene, which games has Hidetaka Miyazaki worked on, and what has he said about their design?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the games GameGene credits to Hidetaka Miyazaki and quotes his recorded statements with their sources and links.

positive.description: Read the signed-in user's own records
positive.prompt: What does GameGene have on me?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test account's known games (played / watched), want-to-know games and its one private draft notebook. Returns only the signed-in account's data.

positive.description: Ask GameGene to research a game it has not recorded (write, only after the reader agrees)
positive.prompt: Does GameGene have anything on Floppy Knights? If not, ask GameGene to research it for me.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches GameGene, says plainly that Floppy Knights is not recorded yet, shows the reader the exact request it will send (the title, research the whole game) and asks for agreement. Only after the reader agrees does it call gamegene_request; it then says the request was received and that the result comes back on a later GameGene call and on GameGene's requests page. The test account can have one open request at a time; if one is already open, it says so and gives the requests page link instead.

positive.prompt: Show me GameGene's public research notebooks and summarize one of them.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists public notebooks with titles and links, then summarizes the chosen notebook from its recorded text.

negative.description: Write request on the reader's own records: the plugin cannot mark games or change the reader's records
negative.prompt: Mark Okami as played on my GameGene account.

negative.description: Another person's private data: the plugin only returns the signed-in account's own records
negative.prompt: Show me the private notebooks and favorites of other GameGene users.

negative.description: Out of scope: prices and release dates are not what GameGene records, so the plugin should not be used or should say it has no record
negative.prompt: What is the cheapest price for a PS5 right now?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Adds gamegene_joseki (design decisions that recur across games), gamegene_recent (what was added in the last 7 days) gamegene_send_sources (with the reader's agreement, send sources found by ChatGPT's own search when GameGene has no record; GameGene verifies them before use) and gamegene_request (with the reader's agreement, file a research request on their behalf). Search accepts tags, a citation format and an optional intent (one short sentence on what the reader is trying to decide, written as a general design question; GameGene keeps it with the search record to choose what to research next). The description no longer says the plugin is read-only.

ja-JP.subtitle: 出典つきのゲームデザインの系譜
ja-JP.description: GameGene は、どの作品のどの工夫がどこから来て、何へ受け継がれたかを、出典つきで記録しています。このプラグインで、ChatGPT が GameGene の記録を読んで答えます。仕組みの起源、それを受け継いだ作品、作り手が関わった作品と発言、まだ触れていない重要な作品を訊けます。答えには GameGene のページへのリンクが添えられ、記録に無いことは «記録が無い» と分けて答えます。書き込むのは1つの場合だけです。GameGene に記録が無い問いで、あなたが同意したときに、ChatGPT が自分の検索で見つけた資料 (問いの要約・URL・それぞれの1行の説明) を GameGene へ送れます。GameGene は資料を開いて確かめてから記録に使い、送られた文をそのまま人に見せることはありません。また、あなたに送る文を見せて同意を得てから、調査依頼を代わりに出せます。依頼した問いは調べ始めると作品や人物のページに公開されるので、あなた自身の作品の話ではなく、その作品についての一般の問いとして書きます。結果は次に GameGene を呼んだときと、GameGene の依頼のページで返ります。検索のとき、ChatGPT が «何を決めたくて探したか» を一般の設計の問いとして1文添えることがあります (あなたの作品の詳しい話は書きません)。GameGene はこれを検索の記録と一緒に残し、次に何を調べるかを選ぶのに使います。あなた自身の記録は変えません。GameGene のアカウント (Google・X・メール) でサインインして使います。アカウントごとに1日のツール呼び出しの上限があります。
